Solar Orbiter factsheet — ESA (body 2.5 x 3.1 x 2.7 m)
First detailed imaging of the Sun's polar regions

ESA-led Solar Orbiter is the first spacecraft designed to image the Sun's polar regions in close detail — using repeated Venus gravity assists over a decade to climb out of the ecliptic toward ~33° heliographic inclination. Carries ten instruments combining remote sensing (PHI magnetograph, EUI extreme-UV imager, SPICE spectrometer, STIX X-ray imager, METIS coronagraph, SoloHI heliospheric imager) with in-situ measurement (magnetometer, energetic particles, solar-wind plasma, radio + plasma waves). Launched 2020-02-10 from Cape Canaveral on a NASA Atlas V 411. First perihelion 2020-06-15 at 0.51 AU. Working perihelion 0.28 AU (~62 R☉), inside Mercury's perihelion distance.
First mission designed to image the Sun's polar regions in detail; complements Parker Solar Probe's in-corona measurements with high-latitude remote sensing
First spacecraft to observe the Sun's poles from above + below the ecliptic — Jupiter gravity assist 1992
First Chinese Mars mission; delivered Zhurong
First mission to the Jupiter Trojans
Twin-orbiter joint ESA + JAXA Mercury mission — splits into MPO + Mio at Mercury arrival in 2026
